newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. spot resids little changed with crude.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. spot resids little changed with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, helped by a fairly well-balanced market, mostly stayed unchanged Wednesday, but trade remained thin as players waited for the onset of summer and better utility demand.

"Fundamentally, I don't see the market getting crushed - there's not a lot of supply around - but, we're still waiting for summer," said one cash trader, noting utility demand has been slack but the market seemed balanced.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held steady at $16.00-25 a barrel, with July one percent paper also unchanged at about $16.10-30, traders said.
While heat this week in the Northeast should stir some load, most agreed it would take a couple of weeks of above normal temperatures to force buyers back into the market.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally inched up by 15-20 cents to about $16.75, but traders said competitive city gate gas prices should limit further gains.
High sulphurs in New York were flat from Tuesday, with 2.2 percent still talked at $14.75-15.00.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent held at $14.50, while one percent was steady to down slightly at about $16.00.
Traders said 50,000 barrels of prompt USG 0.6 percent (low viscosity, high gravity) sold at $15.75 (FOB Miss. River).
USG June three percent paper was still pegged at $14.40.

New York city gate gas prices were unchanged Wednesday in the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, edged up slightly to $2.17/mmBtu, or $13.67 a barrel.
